notes.title: Flinthook review - kinetic platforming that's perfect for Switch
notes.content:
There's a sort of voodoo pelican guy in Flinthook - I think it's voodoo, and I think it's a pelican. Anyway, this guy lobs flaming red skulls at you whenever you meet, and those skulls! Oh my! Those skulls are just the loveliest things. They're like the skulls in Towerfall: 2D art and animation of sufficiently magical quality to convince the mind that you're actually looking at a 3D asset as it spins towards you. I could get hit and killed by those flaming red skulls all day. Just as I could be killed by the insouciant guy who throws blades at you, spreading blades that fly from the hands of an insouciant guy whose very demeanor allows the pixel art to convey with real certainty that this character is definitely French. A French knife-thrower in space, a voodoo pelican with an endless supply of skulls. Flinthook is special.

It is possible when writing about Flinthook, an indie charmer that has just arrived on Switch, to get lost in the unimportant detailing, or rather, to downplay the stuff that really matters in order to explain the mechanical clutter that is drawn so swiftly, so brightly, around the spinning core of a roguelite. Let's get it out of the way here, then.

You're a mysterious space bandit in Flinthook, a game in which the cosmos is filled with wacky creatures flapping around in floating pirate ships. Your job is to take down a range of truly villainous baddies, and you work your way towards each mark by raiding and ultimately exploding a handful of lesser ships which have procedural qualities and their own defining quirks. One might be labyrinthine, for example. One might impose a time limit. As you explore you gain loot and various perks that will aid you on that particular run: you might get an XP boost or immunity from explosions, say. Eventually, you find your target and a boss fight ensues. When you die - and you will - you lose all the temporary perks you gained but you can spend a special kind of gem on permanent character boosting stuff that sees you growing stronger from one game to the next.

notes.title: Dual stick(AKA Pro mode) support - Changelist for r19784
notes.content:
This is a pretty important update. 
We take people's comments seriously. With this one we needed to take our time, digest everyone's input on this and go back to the drawing board. During our prototype phase, we toyed with dual stick controls and couldn't get them to the level of satisfaction we we're looking for.
Regardless, we decided to give it another go. Now that all the pieces of the game are in place, it's easier to take a step back and find the best solution. We still feel like the default option is more accessible but we think giving an option for the more hardcore players is also important. Give it a try for yourself. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25730997/6567421327ccba7ababd057ddd13aea7af242c1d.jpg[/img]

[h1]Changelist for [b]r19784[/b][/h1]

[i]New Features[/i]
[list]
[*]The much requested dual stick mode(AKA Pro mode)!
[/list]

[i]Improvements[/i]
[list]
[*]Added a warning FX to shielded enemies.
[*]Asphyxia and damage over time no longer counts down during end of level minigame.
[*]Stacking featherfall perks can no longer make your gravity zero or negative.
[/list]

[i]Fixes[/i]
[list]
[*]Fixed spikes detaching from moving platforms.
[*]Fixed bubble popping using the buffet FX from time to time.
[*]Prevent bypassing the boss fight in ghost ships.
[*]Fixed Danger Dice when reloading a save.
[*]Fixed button codes in speech bubbles.
[*]Fixed inconsistencies in progression % in the menus for perks, relics and lore.
[*]Minor text fixes
[/list]

notes.title: Changelist for r19724
notes.content:
[i]Improvements[/i]
[list]
[*]Improved hook shot targeting to prioritize bubbles.
[*]Raised the time limit between some damage-over-time effects to -1 hp/20 seconds.
[*]Balanced the ComboBlaster perk to increase critical bonus at a rate of 1%/combo, max of 40% bonus.
[*]Made Midas Blast require less gold to deal extra damage, 2 damage/500 gold.
[*]Made the fire rate reduction on FiercerBlaster less severe, and increase the damage bonus: -40% fire rate/+50% shot damage.
[/list]

[i]Fixes[/i]
[list]
[*]Fixed loc editor. Some characters are not properly supported when publishing.
[*]Fixed daily and weekly challenges timing
[*]Fixed a room where you could be stuck in between walls.
[*]Fixed damage over time effects
[*]Fixed crushers being hidden when re-entering a room.
[*]Fixed launcher validate to check for x86 versions of dependencies.
[*]Minor render priority fixes to the end of level cutscene.
[*]Minor text fixes
[/list]

Flinthook [official site] combines everything I loved about Rogue Legacy with far slicker platforming action, based around some of gaming’s greatest icons: grappling hooks and stylish slow motion. It’s a tremendous game that I’ve been hooked on since launch.

notes.title: Roguelikelike platformer Flinthook swings out
notes.content: Grappling hooks are right up there with strafe-jumping, skateboarding, and swimming on The Official List Of Cool Ways To Move so yes, absolutely let’s peek at Flinthook [official site]. The platformer stars a space pirate who swings through procedurally-generated spaceships, blasting enemies, bopping bosses, and plundering booty. Those space pirates really know how to live! “But Alice,” you wonder, “why do you taunt me so with talk of games that are surely three, six, nine, or eighteen months away from mine own very hands?” Mate, it’s out. You can buy and play it now. Or watch this trailer first: … [visit site to read more]

notes.title: New Trailer + Release Date! April 18!
notes.content:
It’s trailer time! 

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tep1b7jkfyw] [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25730997/a07e48531bf8a5f190cde69c7f6509420374a3a0.jpg[/img] Watch Flinthook's new trailer![/url]

We just released Flinthook’s official gameplay trailer AND have announced the game’s release date - [b]April 18![/b] The game is done, we’re ready to ship it to you all in just a few weeks. Hope you’re ready for some hot hookshot action!

Also - we’re now returning from PAX East, where lots of players got to try Flinthook for the first time. The response was overwhelmingly positive, as players were zipping around spaceships with a smile on their face! Thank you to all who have come to our booth and experienced our demo, it was a joy to see you all.
